summary: Page 14, 'About the town' item within a story on Frank Miller's Newark city commission candidacy, noting fellow prospective candidate Melvin B. Johnson, a former Negro newspaper publisher and editor who left the newspaper business in 1946 to organize Black voters for Gov. Alfred Driscoll's gubernatorial campaign and now works as a public relations assistant in the NJ Department of Labor.

people.name: Melvin B. Johnson
people.role: Former Negro newspaper publisher and editor, of 55 Somerset St., Newark; left newspapers in 1946 for Driscoll campaign work; now public relations assistant, NJ Dept. of Labor; prospective city commission candidate

people.name: Frank Miller
people.role: Former Essex County undersheriff; announced candidacy for Newark City Commission

people.name: Alfred Driscoll
people.role: Governor of New Jersey; Johnson worked among Negro voters for his gubernatorial campaign

people.name: George Reichenstein
people.role: City Clerk, Newark, receiving nominating petitions

incidents.what: Melvin B. Johnson left the Negro newspaper business to work among Negro voters in Gov. Driscoll's gubernatorial campaign
Johnson named as a prospective candidate for Newark City Commission in the May municipal election
